title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Mandatory Comprehensive Credit Reporting) Bill 2018
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Mandatory Comprehensive Credit Reporting) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would make it compulsory for certain lenders to share consumer credit data with credit bureaus.

Eligible licensees that are large authorised deposit-taking institutions as of 1 July 2018 would be required to supply credit information on consumer credit accounts to specified credit reporting bodies.
The bill builds on a voluntary scheme introduced by 2014 amendments to the Privacy Act, and regulations would set conditions for when credit reporting bodies can share or must share the information.
changes: Requires eligible large ADIs to provide credit information on consumer credit accounts to credit reporting bodies.
Establishes a mandatory comprehensive credit reporting regime under the Credit Act.
Allows regulations to set conditions for credit reporting bodies sharing the disclosed information.
summary.affected: Large authorised deposit-taking institutions and other credit providers within their banking group, as well as credit reporting bodies.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Labor supported the mandatory comprehensive credit reporting bill but announced it would move Senate amendments to delay the supply of repayment history information by one year, until after the Attorney-General's Department completes its review of financial hardship arrangements. The scheme requires large banks with assets over $100 billion to share comprehensive credit data, with initial bulk supplies of 50% of accounts due by 28 September 2018 and the remainder by 28 September 2019.
